author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Formation of the Solar System (first solids, CAIs)
summary: Around 4.567 billion years ago, the first solid mineral grains condensed out of the cooling gaseous solar nebula as calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs). Uranium-corrected lead-lead dating of CAIs in carbonaceous chondrites, notably the Allende and Efremovka meteorites, dates their formation to 4567.30 ± 0.16 million years ago, establishing the fundamental 'time-zero' benchmark for the origin of the Solar System and the subsequent accretion of planetesimals and planets.

uncertainty.note: Age is defined by high-precision Pb-Pb isochrons on CAIs in primitive chondrites (4567.30 ± 0.16 Ma by Amelin et al. and 4567.2 ± 0.2 Ma by Burkhardt et al.).

as_recorded.value: accepted age of CAIs of 4567.30 ± 0.16 Ma
start of Solar System history 4567.2±0.2 million years (Myr) ago

where.modern_name: Pueblito de Allende, Chihuahua, Mexico (evidence anchor: fall site of the Allende carbonaceous chondrite meteorite, which yielded benchmark CAIs; event was astronomical across the solar nebula)
where.historical_name: Solar Nebula, circumsolar protoplanetary disk; event predates Earth and all terrestrial landmasses

paleo.not_applicable: Astronomical event in the protoplanetary nebula preceding the formation of Earth, continents, and plate tectonic systems.

importance.justification: The condensation of CAIs at 4567.3 Ma marks 'time-zero' for the birth of the Solar System and all subsequent planetary formation.

related.because: The condensation of CAIs and accretion of chondritic planetesimals produced the rocky material from which Earth subsequently formed.

sources.title: Recent progress and future prospects of the early solar system chronology

reviewer_note: Astronomical event in the proto-planetary disk anchored on Earth to Pueblito de Allende in Chihuahua, Mexico, where thousands of fragments of the CV3 Allende carbonaceous chondrite fell on 8 February 1969, providing the pristine CAIs dated to 4567.3 Ma.
